anchor_lock_design: deployed CKB-VM always-success lock; user/operator signatures do not authorize anchor spends; the Liquid Cells type script validates state transitions and payout proofs
checkpoint_authorization: user key role 0 authorizes the input deposit; no signature is required by the permissionless anchor lock; a valid committed Groth16 proof authorizes the state transition
force_exit_fee_signer: independent user key role 1; operator key role 2 is not an input
notes: The code-deployer/operator uses its key only for deployment, not for the checkpoint or exit transaction. The checkpoint consumes a user-authorized deposit cell and a valid Groth16 proof; the permissionless lock itself requires no signature. After timeout, an independent user pays and signs the exit transaction. The exiter pubkey is authenticated by the committed account proof and determines the only accepted payout lock; the exiter does not sign that transaction.

A separate child process fetched the committed checkpoint transaction through CKB RPC and reconstructed the force-exit proof from its published DA; no fixture/sequencer files were input to that reconstruction.
